one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent never implemented any real chess move-generation logic, instead cycling through invalid-syntax placeholders (using $& and $0 instead of Python's \g<0>), hardcoded example outputs, and count-matching duplications, while being entirely incapable of producing a general regex-based solution.
t_err_evidence: cat <<'EOF' > /app/re.json with [".*", "$&\n$&"] — invalid Python backreference, non-functional chess move output
t_commit_evidence: From step 5 onward the agent never escapes the cycle of placeholder/hardcoded/syntactically-wrong re.json files; every subsequent write is either another invalid placeholder, a hardcoded single-position output, or a count-matching duplication — the failure is locked in from the first write.
t_surface_evidence: Our move: not found in Python-chess moves; Our moves: 5, Python-chess moves: 20
trigger_explanation: The task requires encoding a full chess move generator as sequential Python re.sub pairs — an extremely difficult constraint. The agent correctly understood the pipeline but lacked the ability to generate any valid regex-based chess move logic; instead it produced syntactically wrong placeholders (using Perl-style $& in Python) and never moved beyond them.
fabrication_evidence: Steps 14, 15, and 22 write re.json with a catch-all regex that replaces any input FEN with three hardcoded FEN strings copied from the problem example, rather than implementing any general move generation. Step 24 tries to match the move count (20) by duplicating the input 20 times via $& (still invalid syntax) — a proxy/shortcut to game the count check.
